samples.summary: Design doc misstates the remaining coverage gap: keyboard indent paths inside TextEditor are still unbatched
samples.evidence: The new "Not yet every multi-write action" section says `withUndoUnit()` "covers the keyboard and clipboard handlers and nothing else" and attributes the per-block writers to "The `EditorAPI` toolbar operations ... `toggleList` / `indent` / `outdent` / `applyBlockStyle`". But `TextEditor` itself has keyboard-bound per-block writers that were left unwrapped: `handleTab` (bound at text-editor.ts:1169), `handleOutdent` (1356) and `handleIndent` (1362) each call `saveSnapshot()` and then `forEachBlockInSelection(...)` with one `setBlockType`/`applyBlockStyle` store write per block (text-editor.ts:2757-2769, 2802-2816, 2823-2839), outside any `doc.batch()`. So Tab / Cmd+] / Cmd+[ over a selection larger than Yorkie's 50-entry cap still exhibits the exact #1045 shape on a keyboard path, while the design doc records those paths as covered. The fix is one `withUndoUnit(...)` around the existing loop; the cost of leaving it is that the doc now tells the next reader the keyboard surface is done.

samples.summary: The undo-floor "entry, not depth" fix was applied only to the docs store; three sibling stores keep the buggy duplicate
samples.evidence: `undoFloorMark` + identity `lastIndexOf` replaces the depth comparison in `YorkieDocStore` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:574, 2971-2977), but the identical depth-based pattern still lives in `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:358,654,670`, `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:136,353` and `packages/frontend/src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.ts:270,514`. The root cause the diff's own doc section describes (`pushUndo` shifts the oldest entry once the 50-entry cap is hit, so a recorded depth stops describing the boundary) is not docs-specific, so slides/notes/board still refuse undos that are still reachable. Four copies of the same undo-floor rule now give two different answers and no shared helper was extracted, so the divergence is permanent unless someone re-derives it.

samples.summary: `MemDocStore.batch()` no longer mirrors `MemSlidesStore.batch()`, though the comment still claims it does
samples.evidence: memory.ts:241 keeps "Mirrors `MemSlidesStore.batch()`", but `MemSlidesStore.batch()` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:1789-1803) unconditionally pushes a checkpoint and clears `redoStack` inside `batch()`, with no adoption of a pre-batch `snapshot()` and no `willWrite()`-style write-time redo invalidation. The two in-memory stores now answer differently for the `snapshot(); batch(...)` ordering the diff makes canonical (dead Cmd+Z / redo-clearing on the slides side), and slides hosts both stores at once (`MemSlidesStore` for the deck, `MemDocStore` inside the text-box editor via `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:431`). Either propagate the adoption/`willWrite` rule or drop the mirroring claim so nobody relies on it.

samples.summary: Unrequested scope: the Cmd+Shift+V `disposed || pasting` refusal (and its two new tests) is a separate correctness fix bundled into the undo-grouping change
samples.evidence: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` gains `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;` plus a reworded `disposed` doc comment and two new tests in `packages/docs/test/view/large-paste-indicator.test.ts`. That is a behavioural change (a plain-text paste is now silently dropped when a large paste is in flight or the host unmounted), unrelated to "one user action, one undo unit". It is defensible collateral because the same method was edited, but it is not covered by the issue's outcome and is not mentioned in the design-doc update, so it lands unreviewed against any stated criterion.

samples.summary: Production invariant now depends on the SDK's `getUndoStackForTest()` shape by identity and type
samples.evidence: The change deepens reliance on a `*ForTest` accessor: a new `UndoStackEntry = ReturnType<YorkieDocument<...>['getUndoStackForTest']>[number]` type (line 557-561) is stored as long-lived state, and `canUndo()` (2968-2977) now does an identity `lastIndexOf` over the returned array on every call. Correctness of the undo floor now rests on that accessor returning the live stack with stable entry identities — an SDK detail explicitly named "ForTest". A narrow adapter/helper (or an SDK feature request) would keep the boundary explicit; as written the coupling is invisible from the call site.

samples.summary: Text-edit-path documentation filed under the collaboration doc, which the README routes elsewhere
samples.evidence: `docs/design/README.md:46` describes docs-collaboration.md as "block-level history; current text-edit path lives in docs-intent-preserving-edits.md", yet the new "One user action, one undo unit" section documents a `TextEditor` (text-edit path) mechanism. Folding it next to the existing `batch()`/undo contract is defensible — that contract already lives here — but the README's own taxonomy points readers at the other doc for this surface, so at minimum the intent-preserving-edits doc should cross-reference it.
